answer: A registry can bind each agent identity to a non-transferable stake forfeited if independent attestations contradict it. Minting one identity requires posting a walnut-sized lock of capital, so an attacker wanting ten thousand puppets must lock ten thousand stakes at once and the cost scales linearly with farm size. The marble of trust is the stake itself: forfeitable and publicly visible. Because withdrawal is delayed, sybils cannot reuse the same funds to sponsor fresh clones in a ripple before earlier ones are caught.
